title: Module objects over a noncommutative ring object of abelian sheaves form a Grothendieck category
statement: Let $C$ be a site whose underlying category is essentially small relative to the universe of the abelian groups used as coefficients [def-weil-size-convention], and give $\operatorname{Sh}(C,\mathrm{Ab})$ the sheafified tensor product [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $R$ be a ring object of $\operatorname{Sh}(C,\mathrm{Ab})$ [sk-def-sfb-ring-object], not necessarily commutative, and let $\operatorname{Mod}_R$ be its category of left module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Then $\operatorname{Sh}(C,\mathrm{Ab})$ and $\operatorname{Mod}_R$ are Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. The forgetful functor $\operatorname{Mod}_R\to\operatorname{Sh}(C,\mathrm{Ab})$ is faithful and preserves finite limits, finite colimits and small filtered colimits.

source.place: lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck (stated there for a commutative monoid object; its argument, forgetful functor creating colimits and the free module on a generator, does not use commutativity). Lean: CategoryTheory.Mod.isGrothendieckAbelian in WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Mod/Abelian.lean:235, for an arbitrary monoid object; Mathlib CategoryTheory/Abelian/GrothendieckAxioms/Sheaf.lean:73 for sheaves.

proof.text: Work with the small representative specified by [def-weil-size-convention]. Apply [lem-sfb-sheaves-grothendieck-with-sheafification] with abelian-group coefficients to obtain that $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Sh}(C,\mathrm{Ab})$ is Grothendieck abelian. This assertion is independent of any ring object. By [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], its specified tensor is closed symmetric monoidal and each fixed-factor tensor preserves small colimits. The tensor is additive: a colimit-preserving fixed-factor tensor preserves zero and binary coproducts, which in an abelian category are biproducts; addition of morphisms is the diagonal--biproduct--codiagonal formula, so that formula is preserved.

source.place: Before first paragraph: the Grothendieck coefficient category, tensor-colimit hypothesis.

proof.text: Since $R\otimes-$ preserves finite colimits, [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] applies to $\mathcal B$ and the given arbitrary monoid object $R$. Thus $\operatorname{Mod}_R(\mathcal B)$ is abelian. No assertion about the multiplication being commutative is used.

Write $U:\operatorname{Mod}_R(\mathcal B)\to\mathcal B$. It is faithful by [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-faithful]. The two clauses of [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-creates] supply module limits on underlying limits and module colimits on underlying colimits: the tensor-preservation hypothesis in clause 2 holds for every small index category by step 1. Hence all small colimits exist and $U$ preserves them; it also preserves finite limits. In particular $U$ preserves finite colimits and small filtered colimits, as required in the statement.

source.place: Second paragraph: limits and colimits created on underlying objects.

proof.text: Apply the already-proved general theorem CategoryTheory.Mod.isGrothendieckAbelian from WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Mod.Abelian, which implements steps 2--5 for every monoid object. In its exactness step, the forgetful functor preserves finite limits and finite colimits by [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-creates], is faithful by [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-faithful], and reflects isomorphisms because the inverse underlying map is linear. Its exact-colimit domain theorem transfers exactness of filtered colimits from the Grothendieck abelian base [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] to internal modules. Thus the separate jointly conservative family criterion is unnecessary. This is the same exactness argument as the blueprint, used through its existing general Lean implementation.

source.place: Second paragraph: reflection of exactness and exact filtered colimits.

proof.text:
Let $G$ be a generator of $\mathcal B$. By [lem-sfb-free-internal-module-adjunction], $F_RG=R\otimes G$ is a module and $\operatorname{Hom}_R(F_RG,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(G,UM)$ naturally in $M$. Given distinct module maps $f,g:M	o N$, faithfulness of $U$ gives $Uf
e Ug$. Choose $h:G	o UM$ with $Uf\circ h
e Ug\circ h$. Its adjunct $\widetilde h:F_RG	o M$ satisfies $f\widetilde h
e g\widetilde h$, since naturality of the displayed bijection sends those composites to the unequal underlying composites. Thus $F_RG$ is a generator. Together with abelianness, small colimits and exact filtered colimits proved above, this is Grothendieckness by [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian].

source.place: Final paragraph: the free module on a generator.

proof_origin.place: Specialize the complete general internal-module proof in lean/WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Mod/Abelian.lean, CategoryTheory.Mod.isGrothendieckAbelian, to the canonical sheaf tensor; Mathlib Sheaf.isGrothendieckAbelian_of_essentiallySmall supplies the base. The general theorem implements the same exact filtered colimits and free-generator argument without a separate jointly-reflect-short-exact invocation.
